stories.headline: Tusk announces 'Putin's Five' strategy at Civic Coalition National Council
stories.summary: Prime Minister Donald Tusk delivered a major speech at the Civic Coalition National Council meeting, presenting what he called 'Putin's Five' points against Poland and equating them with Kaczyński's agenda. He also announced a 10-person team to prepare for 2027 elections and selected new party leadership.

stories.headline: Donald Tusk visits South Korea and Japan in historic Asia diplomatic tour
stories.summary: Prime Minister Donald Tusk began a historic visit to Asia, starting in South Korea as the first Polish PM to visit in over 25 years. The trip includes meetings with top officials and discussions on strategic cooperation, Ukraine support, and business partnerships. Japan is next on the itinerary.

stories.headline: Tusk celebrates Hungarian opposition victory over Viktor Orbán
stories.summary: Prime Minister Tusk expressed enthusiasm over Peter Magyar's electoral success in Hungary, calling it a 'magnificent victory' and stating that Hungary, Poland, and Europe are 'together again.' He spoke with Magyar and indicated Poland would be his first foreign destination as Hungarian PM.

stories.headline: Constitutional Tribunal judges oath ceremony sparks political crisis
stories.summary: Six newly elected Constitutional Tribunal judges took their oath in the Sejm without President Nawrocki's participation, causing a major political dispute. Nawrocki only accepted oaths from two judges, while the other four conducted their ceremony independently. Multiple politicians condemned the situation as constitutional crisis.

stories.headline: 16th anniversary of Smolensk air disaster commemorated with calls for 'truth'

stories.headline: NBP reports record 35.7 billion złoty loss while increasing gold reserves to 580 tons
stories.summary: NBP President Adam Glapiński announced the bank's 2025 financial result was negative at 35.7 billion złoty, mainly due to złoty strengthening and inflation-fighting costs. Despite this, NBP increased gold reserves to 580 tons and aims for 700 tons. The bank also reported 169 billion złoty in unrealized gains on gold reserves.

stories.headline: PKN Orlen adjusts fuel prices multiple times amid market volatility
stories.summary: PKN Orlen made several adjustments to wholesale fuel prices throughout the week, with gasoline and diesel prices fluctuating in response to global oil market conditions and the situation in the Middle East. Czech Prime Minister Babiš criticized Orlen for allegedly unjustified price increases despite falling crude oil prices.

stories.headline: Polish Armed Forces to call up to 200,000 people for military exercises in 2026
stories.summary: The Ministry of National Defense announced plans to call up to 200,000 people from passive reserves for military exercises in 2026. The draft regulation sets upper limits for different types of military service. Special emphasis is placed on recruiting people with technical skills like drivers and mechanics.

stories.headline: ABW arrests third Polish citizen in connection with Czech Pardubice factory fire
stories.summary: The Internal Security Agency (ABW) arrested a 23-year-old Polish man in Zielona Góra suspected of assisting in the intentional arson at a defense industry facility in Czech Pardubice. This is the third Polish citizen detained in connection with the March 20 fire at LPP HOLDING, which cooperates with Ukraine's defense industry.

stories.headline: PiS announces new education reforms and Jarosław Kaczyński criticizes current higher education law
stories.summary: PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński announced plans for a new higher education law at a conference in Bydgoszcz, admitting that the current law implemented by his government 'was not one of the best.' The party presented proposals to increase science funding from 1% to 3% of GDP over eight years and emphasized the importance of talent development, especially in AI.
